# Spar 0.5.0

**0.4 gave Spar a learner model. 0.5 is about what you actually look at while
you work: one home instead of three pages, a results panel that shows the
failure instead of burying it, and a grader that stops wasting your time once
it already knows the answer.**

## One home, named by what is live

- **Today and Progress are gone, folded into Home.** They were two pages
  answering one question badly — a recommendation with no argument behind it,
  and a record of everything that had ever happened. Home leads with the
  challenge you are on and the case for it.
- **The ability page argues rather than lists.** What you can now do, what the
  evidence for it is, and what is still uncertain — instead of a timeline you
  have to reconstruct the claim from.
- **Sidebar rows are named by the challenge in progress**, not by the goal you
  typed when you opened the track. Five tracks now read as five different
  lines.
- **Back and forward**, across everything — challenges, abilities, history,
  settings.

## The results panel

- **Every case in the suite is one dot.** A row of chips named "Case 1 · Case
  2 · Case 3" is a list nobody reads; the only questions you have after a run
  are *did it pass* and *which one didn't*, and forty chips answer neither
  until you have scanned all forty.
- **Verdict on the left, evidence on the right.** Stacked, the panel used to
  spend its whole height before saying anything — a verdict line, a square of
  dots, the case name, an Input pane — and the two values you came for were
  below the fold. None of that is long, it is just tall, and all of it is
  narrow.
- **Input stopped being a third pane.** It picks its own weight now: nothing
  reported draws nothing, a short input is one line under the case name, and a
  long or multi-line one still gets the full block.
- **The other failures are listed by name.** Six red dots are six identical
  marks. Six names are a pattern, and the pattern is usually the bug — every
  failing case is an empty input, or every one of them is negative.

## Submissions stop at the first failure

The hidden suite is a grader. Once one case fails the submission is already
rejected, and the two hundred verdicts after it are noise you read past to find
the one that mattered. Visible runs are unchanged — that list is the contract
you are working against, so all of it runs and all of it reports.

## Step back through a session

A session is a run of challenges, and until now only the last one was
reachable. Everything before it had been solved and put away, and the only way
back was the global history list — every challenge you have ever done, which is
the wrong list for "the one before this".

## Fixes and polish

- **Maths in chat renders as maths.** A complexity review saying the bound is
  `\(O(1)\)` used to print the delimiters literally: the one piece of notation
  in the sentence arrived as syntax.
- **Challenges record what they replace.** A revised challenge kept no link to
  the one it replaced, so a session read as a flat list of unrelated problems
  rather than as a chain with revisions in it.
- **A fresh install no longer fails to open its database.** An index was
  created over a column that a migration added afterwards — invisible on any
  store that already had the column, fatal on a new one.
- **Hints published by a practice source fold shut** instead of sitting beside
  a problem you did not ask them for.
- **The problem header leads with the problem's name.**

## Downloads

| Your machine | File |
| --- | --- |
| Mac, Apple silicon | `Spar-0.5.0-arm64.dmg` |
| Mac, Intel | `Spar-0.5.0.dmg` |
| Windows | `Spar-0.5.0-x64.exe` |
| Linux | `Spar-0.5.0-x86_64.AppImage` or `Spar-0.5.0-amd64.deb` |

## Known limits

- This open distribution is unsigned. macOS Gatekeeper or Windows SmartScreen
  may ask you to approve the first launch, and those platforms may require a
  manual installer step for an update.
- Linux AppImage installations can self-update when the runtime supports it;
  `.deb` installations remain managed by the system package manager.
